cues.text: Hello, little ones. Come sit with me by the fire. Get cozy now... that's it. Tonight I want to tell you about a president. A president is the person who takes care of the whole country — that's a very big job. And this president lived a long, long time ago, back when your great-great-grandparents were little. His name was Franklin. And back then, the country was having a very hard time. Lots of mommies and daddies couldn't find work, and lots of families were worried. Worried about dinner. Worried about tomorrow. Now, Franklin couldn't visit every house. There were too many houses! So do you know what he did? He sat down in front of a little brown radio — just like this one right here — and he talked. Right into the radio. And his voice traveled through the air, all across the country, into kitchens and living rooms everywhere. He said, 'Hello, my friends.' And then he explained everything, slow and simple, so everyone could understand. He told them: don't be afraid. We will figure this out together. And you know what? Families gathered around their radios, just like you're gathered around me. And they felt a little braver. Because sometimes, when someone kind talks to you, the worry gets a little smaller. So here's what I want you to remember tonight: your voice is powerful. When someone you love feels scared, you can sit with them, talk soft and kind, and help their worry get smaller too. Now... who wants a story about a brave little mouse next time?
